manifest.title: Compositional polynomial-time computation with black-box subroutines

inputs.abstract:
Polynomial-time algorithms can be combined using implementations supplied
only by existence theorems. We give a structured stack language with calls
to a fixed library of input/output contracts and compile it to ordinary
finite stack Turing machines. Calls preserve the caller's other stacks and
finite control, and reset all private storage. Their exact cost is the
callee's running time plus two traversals of each argument and result and
four transfer transitions.

Polynomial bounds on source execution and on call argument and result sizes
give polynomial bounds on the compiled machine. The resulting interface
supports sequencing, conditionals, loops, and adaptive calls inside verified
programs. As a direct public corollary, encoded polynomial-time functions are
closed under sequential composition, even when their implementations are
supplied only by existence theorems.

concepts.title: Composition of polynomial-time algorithms
concepts.description:
Encoded polynomial-time functions can be used through their existential
machine witnesses. Their outputs have polynomially bounded encoded size,
and composition preserves polynomial time. All size measures refer to the
specified encodings; the intermediate encoding is shared by both algorithms.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax218471.PolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Composition of polynomial-time algorithms
type: theorem
---
Encoded polynomial-time functions can be used through their existential
machine witnesses. Their outputs have polynomially bounded encoded size,
and composition preserves polynomial time. All size measures refer to the
specified encodings; the intermediate encoding is shared by both algorithms.
-/

namespace Lax218471.Combinators

open PolynomialTime

/-- Every polynomial-time function has polynomially bounded output size. -/
axiom output_size {α β A B : Type} {ea : α → List A} {eb : β → List B} {f : α → β}
    (h : Polytime ea eb f) :
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, ∀ a, (eb (f a)).length ≤ p.eval (ea a).length

/-- An existential polynomial-time algorithm realizes its encoded contract. -/
axiom graph_realizable {α β A : Type} {ea : α → List A} {eb : β → List A} {f : α → β}
    (h : Polytime ea eb f) : Nonempty (Implementation (Graph ea eb f))

/-- Sequential composition of algorithms supplied only by existence statements. -/
axiom comp {α β γ A : Type} [Fintype A] [Inhabited A]
    {ea : α → List A} {eb : β → List A} {ec : γ → List A}
    {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} (hf : Polytime ea eb f) (hg : Polytime eb ec g) :
    Polytime ea ec (g ∘ f)

end Lax218471.Combinators

statements.signature:
comp : ∀ {α β γ A : Type} [Fintype A] [Inhabited A] {ea : α → List A} {eb : β → List A} {ec : γ → List A} {f : α → β}
  {g : β → γ},
  Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Polytime ea eb f →
    Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Polytime eb ec g → Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Polytime ea ec (Function.comp g f)
statements.doc: Sequential composition of algorithms supplied only by existence statements.

  Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Polytime ea eb f →
    Nonempty (Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Implementation (Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Graph ea eb f))

concepts.title: Polynomial-time implementations of encoded functions and contracts
concepts.description:
Polynomial time is measured in the length of the specified input encoding.
An implementation contains an actual finite TM2 and a polynomial time bound.
A contract may restrict the valid inputs: callers must establish the contract
at every call. This permits direct use of algorithms whose correctness is
known only on well-formed encodings.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Computability.TuringMachine.Computable

/-!
---
title: Polynomial-time implementations of encoded functions and contracts
type: definition
---
Polynomial time is measured in the length of the specified input encoding.
An implementation contains an actual finite TM2 and a polynomial time bound.
A contract may restrict the valid inputs: callers must establish the contract
at every call. This permits direct use of algorithms whose correctness is
known only on well-formed encodings.
-/

namespace Lax218471.PolynomialTime

open Turing

/-- Existence of a finite machine computing an encoded function in polynomial time. -/
def Polytime {α β A B : Type} (ea : α → List A) (eb : β → List B) (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea eb f)

/-- A finite machine and a time bound realizing every input/output pair of a contract. -/
structure Implementation {A : Type} (R : List A → List A → Prop) extends
    TM2ComputableAux A A where
  time : Polynomial ℕ
  correct : ∀ x y, R x y →
    Nonempty (TM2OutputsInTime tm (x.map inputAlphabet.symm)
      (some (y.map outputAlphabet.symm)) (time.eval x.length))

/-- The input/output relation of an encoded function. -/
def Graph {α β A : Type} (ea : α → List A) (eb : β → List A) (f : α → β)
    (x y : List A) : Prop := ∃ a, ea a = x ∧ eb (f a) = y

end Lax218471.PolynomialTime

concepts.title: Structured stack programs with black-box calls
concepts.description:
Programs use stack operations, finite control, sequencing, conditionals,
while loops, and calls to a fixed library of contracts. A call replaces one
stack with its result and preserves every other stack and the caller's control.
The execution relation records the number of source instructions and a bound
on all call argument and result lengths. In particular, a polynomial bound
on the number of iterations alone does not assert polynomial time.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax218471.Subroutine
import Lax218471.PolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Structured stack programs with black-box calls
type: definition
---
Programs use stack operations, finite control, sequencing, conditionals,
while loops, and calls to a fixed library of contracts. A call replaces one
stack with its result and preserves every other stack and the caller's control.
The execution relation records the number of source instructions and a bound
on all call argument and result lengths. In particular, a polynomial bound
on the number of iterations alone does not assert polynomial time.
-/

namespace Lax218471.Programs

open Subroutine

variable {K A σ I : Type}

/-- One local operation; the control type is finite when programs are compiled. -/
inductive Op (K A σ : Type)
  | push (k : K) (f : σ → A)
  | pop (k : K) (f : σ → Option A → σ)
  | peek (k : K) (f : σ → Option A → σ)
  | load (f : σ → σ)

/-- A finite program with named library calls. Loops retain their body as finite code. -/
inductive Program (K A σ I : Type)
  | atom (o : Op K A σ)
  | call (i : I) (port : K)
  | seq (p q : Program K A σ I)
  | branch (b : σ → Bool) (p q : Program K A σ I)
  | loop (b : σ → Bool) (p : Program K A σ I)

def Op.apply [DecidableEq K] (o : Op K A σ) (s : Store (fun _ : K => A) σ) :
    Store (fun _ : K => A) σ :=
  match o with
  | .push k f => ⟨s.state, Function.update s.stk k (f s.state :: s.stk k)⟩
  | .pop k f => ⟨f s.state (s.stk k).head?, Function.update s.stk k (s.stk k).tail⟩
  | .peek k f => ⟨f s.state (s.stk k).head?, s.stk⟩
  | .load f => ⟨f s.state, s.stk⟩

/-- Source execution, with a bound on the length of every argument and reply. -/
inductive Executes [DecidableEq K] (R : I → List A → List A → Prop) (size : ℕ) :
    Program K A σ I → Store (fun _ : K => A) σ → Store (fun _ : K => A) σ → ℕ → Prop
  | atom (o) (s) : Executes R size (.atom o) s (o.apply s) 1
  | call (i) (port) (s) (y) : R i (s.stk port) y →
      (s.stk port).length ≤ size → y.length ≤ size →
      Executes R size (.call i port) s ⟨s.state, Function.update s.stk port y⟩ 1
  | seq {p q s u t a b} : Executes R size p s u a → Executes R size q u t b →
      Executes R size (.seq p q) s t (a + b)
  | branch_true {p q s t a} {b : σ → Bool} : b s.state = true →
      Executes R size p s t a → Executes R size (.branch b p q) s t (a + 1)
  | branch_false {p q s t a} {b : σ → Bool} : b s.state = false →
      Executes R size q s t a → Executes R size (.branch b p q) s t (a + 1)
  | loop_false {p s} {b : σ → Bool} : b s.state = false →
      Executes R size (.loop b p) s s 1
  | loop_true {p s u t a c} {b : σ → Bool} : b s.state = true →
      Executes R size p s u a → Executes R size (.loop b p) u t c →
      Executes R size (.loop b p) s t (a + c + 1)

end Lax218471.Programs

concepts.title: Finite stack subroutines and their interfaces
concepts.description:
A subroutine has access to the caller's stacks and finite control, together
with a private finite collection of working stacks and private finite control.
At entry and return its private stacks are empty and its private control is
reset. Execution counts actual TM2 transitions. This interface makes repeated
calls and preservation of unrelated caller data explicit.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Computability.TuringMachine.Computable
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sum
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod

/-!
---
title: Finite stack subroutines and their interfaces
type: definition
---
A subroutine has access to the caller's stacks and finite control, together
with a private finite collection of working stacks and private finite control.
At entry and return its private stacks are empty and its private control is
reset. Execution counts actual TM2 transitions. This interface makes repeated
calls and preservation of unrelated caller data explicit.
-/

namespace Lax218471.Subroutine

open Turing

/-- The data visible to a caller between subroutine calls. -/
structure Store {K : Type} (Γ : K → Type) (σ : Type) where
  state : σ
  stk : ∀ k, List (Γ k)

/-- An ordinary finite TM2 program with a private working region. -/
structure Routine {K : Type} (Γ : K → Type) (σ : Type) where
  W : Type
  [workEq : DecidableEq W]
  [workFin : Fintype W]
  Δ : W → Type
  τ : Type
  [stateFin : Fintype τ]
  initial : τ
  Label : Type
  [labelFin : Fintype Label]
  entry : Label
  code : Label → TM2.Stmt (Sum.elim Γ Δ) Label (σ × τ)

namespace Routine

variable {K σ : Type} {Γ : K → Type} (p : Routine Γ σ)

instance : DecidableEq p.W := p.workEq
instance : Fintype p.W := p.workFin
instance : Fintype p.τ := p.stateFin
instance : Fintype p.Label := p.labelFin

/-- A boundary configuration contains no private working data. -/
def boundary (l : Option p.Label) (s : Store Γ σ) :
    TM2.Cfg (Sum.elim Γ p.Δ) p.Label (σ × p.τ) where
  l := l
  var := (s.state, p.initial)
  stk := fun | .inl k => s.stk k | .inr _ => []

/-- Exact execution from a clean entry to a clean return. -/
def Executes [DecidableEq K] (s t : Store Γ σ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (fun c => c.bind (TM2.step p.code))^[n] (some (p.boundary (some p.entry) s)) =
    some (p.boundary none t)

end Routine
end Lax218471.Subroutine

concepts.title: Polynomial-time substitution of black-box subroutines
concepts.description:
A structured program with a fixed library of polynomial-time subroutines
compiles to an ordinary finite stack Turing machine. Every call includes
argument transfer, execution of the supplied machine, output transfer, and
cleanup of private storage. A bound on source instructions and on every
argument and reply yields a polynomial bound on actual machine execution.

The library is chosen before the input. Its implementations may be supplied
existentially by other theorems. Calls may be adaptive and may occur inside
loops, provided the execution proof supplies the stated uniform size bound.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax218471.Programs

/-!
---
title: Polynomial-time substitution of black-box subroutines
type: theorem
---
A structured program with a fixed library of polynomial-time subroutines
compiles to an ordinary finite stack Turing machine. Every call includes
argument transfer, execution of the supplied machine, output transfer, and
cleanup of private storage. A bound on source instructions and on every
argument and reply yields a polynomial bound on actual machine execution.

The library is chosen before the input. Its implementations may be supplied
existentially by other theorems. Calls may be adaptive and may occur inside
loops, provided the execution proof supplies the stated uniform size bound.
-/

namespace Lax218471.Substitution

open Subroutine Programs PolynomialTime

/-- Compilation to a concrete subroutine, with polynomial overhead per source
instruction in the maximum call argument and reply length. -/
axiom compile {K A σ I : Type} [DecidableEq K] [Fintype A] [Inhabited A]
    (R : I → List A → List A → Prop)
    (library : ∀ i, Nonempty (Implementation (R i))) (p : Program K A σ I) :
    ∃ (r : Routine (fun _ : K => A) σ) (overhead : Polynomial ℕ),
      ∀ size s t n, Executes R size p s t n →
        ∃ m ≤ n * overhead.eval size, r.Executes s t m

/-- The caller's initial or final store, with a single designated data stack. -/
def ioStore {K A σ : Type} [DecidableEq K]
    (port : K) (initial : σ) (xs : List A) : Store (fun _ : K => A) σ :=
  ⟨initial, Function.update (fun _ => []) port xs⟩

/-- Polynomially many source instructions and polynomially bounded calls
suffice for polynomial-time computation by an actual finite TM2. -/
axiom polytime {K A σ I : Type} [DecidableEq K] [Fintype A] [Inhabited A]
    [Fintype K] [Fintype σ] {α β : Type}
    (R : I → List A → List A → Prop)
    (library : ∀ i, Nonempty (Implementation (R i))) (p : Program K A σ I)
    (input output : K) (initial : σ) (ea : α → List A) (eb : β → List A) (f : α → β)
    (steps size : Polynomial ℕ)
    (h : ∀ a, ∃ n ≤ steps.eval (ea a).length,
      Executes R (size.eval (ea a).length) p
        (ioStore input initial (ea a)) (ioStore output initial (eb (f a))) n) :
    Polytime ea eb f

end Lax218471.Substitution

statements.signature:
compile : ∀ {K A σ I : Type} [inst : DecidableEq K] [Fintype A] [Inhabited A] (R : I → List A → List A → Prop),
  (∀ (i : I), Nonempty (Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Implementation (R i))) →
    ∀ (p : Lax218471.Programs.Program K A σ I),
      Exists fun r =>
        Exists fun overhead =>
          ∀ (size : Nat) (s t : Lax218471.Subroutine.Store (fun x => A) σ) (n : Nat),
            Lax218471.Programs.Executes R size p s t n →
              Exists fun m => And (instLENat.le m (instHMul.hMul n (Polynomial.eval size overhead))) (r.Executes s t m)
statements.doc:
Compilation to a concrete subroutine, with polynomial overhead per source
instruction in the maximum call argument and reply length.

statements.signature:
polytime : ∀ {K A σ I : Type} [inst : DecidableEq K] [Fintype A] [Inhabited A] [Fintype K] [Fintype σ] {α β : Type}
  (R : I → List A → List A → Prop),
  (∀ (i : I), Nonempty (Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Implementation (R i))) →
    ∀ (p : Lax218471.Programs.Program K A σ I) (input output : K) (initial : σ) (ea : α → List A) (eb : β → List A)
      (f : α → β) (steps size : Polynomial Nat),
      (∀ (a : α),
          Exists fun n =>
            And (instLENat.le n (Polynomial.eval (ea a).length steps))
              (Lax218471.Programs.Executes R (Polynomial.eval (ea a).length size) p
                (Lax218471.Substitution.ioStore input initial (ea a))
                (Lax218471.Substitution.ioStore output initial (eb (f a))) n)) →
        Lax218471.PolynomialTime.Polytime ea eb f

Polynomially many source instructions and polynomially bounded calls
suffice for polynomial-time computation by an actual finite TM2.
